title: The Fate of Every Hashira in Demon Slayer Explained
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the Demon Slayer manga! Right after the finale of the Hashira Training Arc , Demon Slayer announced a trilogy of films to adapt the Infinity Castle Arc , the longest and most intense arc in the manga. The final phase of the manga is split into two parts: the Infinity Castle and the Sunrise Countdown . While it’s unclear if the Sunrise Countdown will be adapted into a movie or a TV season, at the very least, fans can expect to enjoy all the exciting fights in the Infinity Castle Arc on the big screen. The anime released the first installment of the trilogy last year, and it became a smashing hit all across the globe.

However, while the anime has yet to adapt a majority of the story, the manga has long since reached its conclusion. Demon Slayer ‘s finale was extremely controversial at the time due to many tragic deaths that happened during the final battle against the demons. As the strongest in the entire Corps, the Hashira have always been on the front lines, and the final battle wasn’t any different.

9) Kyojuro Rengoku

Rengoku is the first Hashira to die in the series, and it happened long before the final battle. During the Mugen Train Arc , Tanjiro and the others joined him on a mission to defeat the demon responsible for the missing passengers inside the Infinity Train. As the Flame Hashira, it goes without saying just how powerful Rengoku was. However, even his overwhelming strength wasn’t enough against the Third Upper Moon. While the mission itself was a huge success with no casualties, no one anticipated the appearance of Akaza.

Not to mention, he wasn’t anything like the Lower Moons, and the difference in their powers was astounding. Rengoku made sure that no one else would have to fight the Upper Three and held on until dawn. Even with a hole in his chest, Rengoku adjusted his breathing and kept fighting to protect everyone until the end. His death is one of the most emotional moments in the series as it gives Tanjiro and the others the push they needed to become stronger.

8) Tengen Uzui

As the Sound Hashira, Uzui had a crucial role in the Entertainment District Arc. Right after the Mugen Train Arc, when Tanjiro and his friends were training diligently, they came across Uzui, who was looking for lower-ranking Demon Slayers to help with a mission. Following a series of events, Uzui and the others ended up fighting Upper Moon Six, Gyutaro, who shared his powers with his sister Daki. The fight was brutal, and the animation is still unmatched .

He suffered grave injuries, including poisoning, losing his left hand and eye. As a dual sword wielder, continuing to work as a Demon Slayer would’ve been increasingly difficult. Although he could’ve chosen to go down the dangerous path, he decided to retire peacefully and live the rest of his life with his wives. As a Shinobi turned Demon Slayer, Uzui spent most of his life fighting, but he finally managed to live on his own terms. He continued to help the Corps out with training and protecting Nezuko during the battle.

7) Shinobu Kocho

Shinobu is not only the Insect Hashira, but also the backbone of the Corps thanks to her extensive knowledge of poisons and medical treatment. Her Butterfly Mansion houses the injured Slayers, where she oversees their treatment and rehabilitation. This makes her one of the most crucial figures in the Corps. Her biggest goal was to find a way to defeat Doma, the Upper Rank Two who killed her sister. Shinobu came face to face with the demon in the Infinity Castle Arc. It was the first major fight in the entire arc, and it ended with her tragic death.

Despite giving it her all, she was unable to defeat the demon and ended up being absorbed by him. That horrifying scene was witnessed by Kanao Tsuyuri , her Tsuguko and adoptive sister. Even after her death, she continues to remain relevant in the story as her real plan comes to light. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that without her, Doma and Muzan’s defeat might have been impossible.

6) Muichiro Tokito

Although Muichiro is the youngest Hashira , his potential is better than most of the cast thanks to his lineage of being a direct descendant of the Sun Breathing Technique. During the Swordsmith Village Arc, he regained his memories and mourned the family he once had. He also awakened his Demon Slayer Mark and effortlessly killed Gyokko, the Upper Rank Five. Considering how much trouble Gyutaro gave to Uzui and the others, Muichiro’s victory was nothing short of marvelous. Just like the rest of the Demon Slayers, he was trapped inside the Infinity Castle, where he used his new powers against Upper One.

It goes without saying that the second most powerful demon in history was more than he could handle. Even with the help of Sanemi, Gyomei, and Genya, the fight was overly intense. Muichiro had one of the most brutal deaths in the series as Kokushibo cut him in half. Even in his dying breath, he landed one final blow to the villain, which paved the path for others to defeat him. After the Infinity Castle collapsed, the surviving Demon Slayers engaged in a battle against Muzan, leaving them with no chance of retrieving the young Hashira’s body.

5) Mitsuri Kanroji

Mitsuri is another Hashira who joined the battle against the Upper Moons in the Swordsmith Village Arc. While Muichiro defeated Gyokko, Mitsuri helped Tanjiro and the others against Hantengu, the Upper Four. She also awakened her Demon Slayer Mark during the battle, which basically saved her life from the powerful demon. She was one of the few survivors in the Infinity Castle Arc, but her luck ran out during the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji. She sustained severe injuries and blood loss because of the demon progenitor.

Not only that, but both her arms were sliced off, leaving her unable to continue fighting. She managed to stay alive for a little while until Obanai returned to her after fighting Muzan. While she couldn’t live the rest of her life with him like she wanted, she confessed her feelings to him, hoping to marry Obanai if they ever got reincarnated. After she heard Obanai promise her that, she drew her final breath in his arms.

4) Obanai Iguro

Obanai and Mitsuri were together the entire time they were trapped inside the Infinity Castle. They fought against Nakime, the newly appointed Upper Four, whose Blood Demon Art manifested the Infinity Castle. After the Infinity Castle Arc, Obanai joined the others during the final battle against Muzan. He also witnessed Mitsuri’s weakened state and knew she wouldn’t survive all those horrifying injuries. Despite knowing he wouldn’t survive the battle, he charged towards Muzan, hoping to do as much damage as possible. Obanai lost his eyesight because of the villain but never stopped fighting him.

His Demon Slayer Mark gave him a slight edge, but it wasn’t enough to help him survive. After the battle was over, he reunited with Mitsuri and succumbed to his injuries a few moments later. They both died at the same time after making a promise that was the only hope they wanted to hold on to, even though they knew it might never come true.

3) Gyomei Himejima

While the anime has long since confirmed that Gyomei is the strongest Hashira, the Infinity Castle Arc will finally explain the true extent of his overwhelming powers. Gyomei teamed with Muichiro, Sanemi, and Genya to fight the Upper Rank One. Kokushibo has been alive for a few centuries, and he’s easily the most powerful demon after Muzan. Kokushibo’s powers were unlike anything the other Upper Ranks were capable of, including Doma and Akaza. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark even though he was past the lethal age, which meant that his time was limited.

While he survived the battle against Kokushibo, Gyomei suffered severe injuries during his fight with Muzan. He lost his leg on top of other injuries and blood loss. Despite that, he ensured that he kept Muzan chained down until sunrise. Gyomei drew his final breath after the battle was over. He also regained his memories of the time he took care of orphans. After remembering that the children didn’t betray him but wanted to protect him from the demon instead, he finally gained peace after all these years.

2) Sanemi Shinazugawa

Sanemi is one of the few surviving Corps members, but the series never revealed if he died after he turned 25. Sanemi was only 21 years old at the time, so he could’ve still had a few years to live. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark during the battle against Kokushibo, and his efforts ensured the demon’s victory. However, Sanemi also lost the only family he had and carried the weight of that loss for the rest of his life.

While Sanemi kept pushing Genya away to protect him, all the younger brother wanted was his forgiveness. Sanemi also fought against Muzan during the final battle and lived to see the demon’s demise. After the Corps was disbanded, he lived the rest of his days in peace while keeping in touch with Tanjiro through letters.

1) Giyu Tomioka

Giyu is another Hashira who survived the battle against Muzan. Following his battle against Akaza, Giyu and Tanjiro were both unable to continue fighting other demons for a while. However, after the Infinity Castle collapsed, Giyu once again used his powers to protect as many people as he could. He joined hands with Tanjiro once again to defeat the final villain and sustained severe injuries in the process. Giyu also lost his arm, but he never gave up fighting.

The night-long battle ended in the Corps’ victory, but barely anyone survived to celebrate the historic moment. Just like Sanemi, Giyu was also 21 years old at the time, so it’s hinted that he could’ve died in four years. However, the series never officially confirmed his death, and much about the Mark and its history isn’t known either. Following the disbandment of the Corps, he lived a solitary life while keeping in touch with his former comrades.

title: Blue Eye Samurai Confirms Final Season Release With New Season 2 Trailer
content:
In 2023, Netflix created one of the most critically acclaimed animated series to ever arrive on the streaming service: Blue Eye Samurai . While a second season has been known to arrive on the platform for some time, many fans were wondering what the future would hold for Mizu and her quest for vengeance. In a good news/bad news reveal, Blue Eye Samurai has been confirmed for a third season, but season three is set to be its last. On top of this major confirmation, a new trailer has arrived for season two, and Netflix has let fans know when we can expect Mizu to end her story.

To start, Blue Eye Samurai’s second season is set for a release window of January 2027, bringing Mizu to London, England, to extend her quest for revenge. While a specific release date has yet to be revealed, Netflix did drop the first full trailer to give fans an idea of what is to come. While the season two news was big enough on its own, perhaps the bigger news was that season three was set to be the final season of Blue Eye Samurai . Luckily, viewers won’t have to wait nearly as long between these future seasons, as the grand finale is set to arrive in 2028. You can check out the brand-new trailer below.

Blue Eye Samurai Original Plans

The news about Blue Eye Samurai’s third season being its last is a departure from what the animated show’s co-creators have been saying in recent years. In previous interviews, creators Amber Noizumi and Michael Green hinted at the idea that they were aiming to tell Mizu’s story over four seasons and a movie. On top of these future projects, Green and Noizumi were also hopeful that the animated series would receive a spin-off focusing on the handless sidekick Ringo. It’s possible that this spin-off could still happen in the future, though for now, nothing has been confirmed by the creators or Netflix as of the writing of this article.

So what can we expect from the second season of Blue Eye Samurai ? As a refresher, the last time we saw Mizu, she was making progress in terms of her bloody quest for revenge, but is now leaving Japan behind and venturing to the United Kingdom. While Mizu had defeated Abijah Fowler, the big bad of season one, there were still several targets that she needed to exact vengeance upon. If the first season is any indication, expect there to be plenty of sword-slinging violence and bloodshed that will be a part of season two. Ironically enough, if one review that dropped last year is any indication , viewers are in for a wild ride in 2027.

title: 'Kikansha no Mahou wa Tokubetsu desu 2nd Season' Reveals New Staff, First Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Yu So-nan and Uk-jakga 's Kikansha no Mahou wa Tokubetsu desu ( A Returner's Magic Should Be Special ) manhwa revealed new staff and the first promotional video for its second season on Friday. The anime will air in October 2026 every Thursday at 12.45 a.m. on Fuji TV's +Ultra programming block.

Staff Director: Taishi Kawaguchi ( Kowloon Generic Romance episode director) Series Composition, Script: Takamitsu Kouno ( Saikyou no Ousama, Nidome no Jinsei wa Nani wo Suru? ) Character Design: Hiromi Katou ( Hametsu no Oukoku ) Art Director: Daisuke Negishi ( Fuguushoku "Kanteishi" ga Jitsu wa Saikyou Datta ) NEW Art Design: Satoshi Fujimoto ( Mebius Dust assistant art director) NEW , Taiga Saitou NEW , Gaku Mukai NEW , Tetsuo Imaizumi ( Kimi wo Aishita Hitori no Boku e background art) NEW Prop Design: Shoutarou Hashiguchi ( Monster Musume no Oishasan chief animation director) Color Design: Aiko Matsuyama ( Grand Blue ) Director of Photography: Hideki Imaizumi ( Mahou no Shimai Lulutto Lilly ) Editing: Gou Sadamatsu ( Tondemo Skill de Isekai Hourou Meshi ) NEW Music: Kenta Higashiooji ( Pole Princess!! Movie ) Sound Director: Takatoshi Hamano ( Yuusha Party wo Oidasareta Kiyoubinbou ) Sound Effects: Yasumasa Koyama ( Fate/strange Fake ) Sound Production: Magic Capsule Studio: Arvo Animation Production: Hayate NEW

Note: The staff denoted with the legend NEW are new in their respective roles.

Produced by Arvo Animation, the first season aired for 12 episodes in Fall 2023. Crunchyroll simulcast the anime with subtitles outside of Asia and subsequently began streaming an English dub.

Yu penned the action fantasy web novel in KakaoPage between September 2016 and August 2019. Yu and Uk-jakga began serializing the manhwa on the same platform in May 2018. D&C Media released the seventh volume in March 2025.

Tappytoon began publishing the manhwa in English digitally in June 2020. Yen Press licensed the series in English for physical release in October 2021 and shipped the sixth volume on April 28.

The web magazine and app Piccoma has been serializing the manhwa in Japan since July 2019. Kadokawa published the third physical volume in October 2023.

title: A Returner's Magic Should Be Special 2nd Season Anime's 1st Promo Video Streamed
content:
The staff for the second season of the anime based on Wookjakga 's A Returner's Magic Should Be Special ( Kikansha no Mahō wa Tokubetsu Desu in Japanese) Korean webtoon revealed its first promotional video on Friday. The anime's website also revealed that it will get an advance screening at Shinjuku Wald 9 in Tokyo on October 3.

The new season will premiere in Fuji TV 's " +Ultra " programming block in October, and it will run on Wednesdays at 24:45 (effectively, Thursdays at 12:45 a.m.). The first season began re-airing on Fuji TV and Kansai TV in July.

Crunchyroll will stream the new season.

The rock band FLOW returns to create the "Sorrow" song specifically for the new season's opening theme. krage will perform the ending theme song "Everlasting."

The anime's cast includes:

• Takuma Terashima as Desir Herman

• Sayumi Suzushiro as Romantica Eru

• Natsumi Fujiwara as Pram Schnaizer

• Asami Seto as Azrest Kingscrown

Taishi Kawaguchi returns to direct the anime at Arvo Animation . Takamitsu Kouno ( She Professed Herself Pupil of the Wise Man , Absolute Duo , We Without Wings - Under the Innocent Sky ) returns to compose the series and write the scripts for the anime. Hiromi Katō ( Violinist of Hamelin , Kobato. , Irina: The Vampire Cosmonaut ) is designing the characters. Daisuke Negishi is the art director. Kenta Higashiohji ( Pole Princess!! ) returns to compose the music.

Other staff include:

• Art design: Satoshi Fujimoto, Taiga Saitō, Takeshi Mukai, Tetsuo Imaizumi

• Prop design: Shōtarō Hashiguchi

• Color design: Aiko Matsuyama

• Director of photography: Hideki Imaizumi

• Editing: Gō Sadamatsu

• Sound director: Takatoshi Hamano

• Sound effects: Yasumasa Koyama

Yen Press is releasing the series in English and it describes the story:

In a time when the Shadow World has taken over and most of humanity is wiped out, a party of six heroes strives and fails to save the world… But magician Desir Herman is given a second chance when he opens his eyes and finds that he's gone back thirteen years in the past! It's now up to him to gather his party once more and stop the greatest catastrophe in human history!

The first season of the anime debuted in October 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired in English-speaking, Latin America, and European countries, along with an English dub .

The new season will premiere in Fuji TV 's " +Ultra " programming block in October, and it will run on Wednesdays at 24:45 (effectively, Thursdays at 12:45 a.m.). The first season began re-airing on Fuji TV and Kansai TV in July.
Crunchyroll will stream the new season.
The rock band FLOW returns to create the "Sorrow" song specifically for the new season's opening theme. krage will perform the ending theme song "Everlasting."
The anime's cast includes:
Takuma Terashima as Desir Herman
Sayumi Suzushiro as Romantica Eru
Natsumi Fujiwara as Pram Schnaizer
Asami Seto as Azrest Kingscrown

Taishi Kawaguchi returns to direct the anime at Arvo Animation . Takamitsu Kouno ( She Professed Herself Pupil of the Wise Man , Absolute Duo , We Without Wings - Under the Innocent Sky ) returns to compose the series and write the scripts for the anime. Hiromi Katō ( Violinist of Hamelin , Kobato. , Irina: The Vampire Cosmonaut ) is designing the characters. Daisuke Negishi is the art director. Kenta Higashiohji ( Pole Princess!! ) returns to compose the music.
Other staff include:
Art design: Satoshi Fujimoto, Taiga Saitō, Takeshi Mukai, Tetsuo Imaizumi
Prop design: Shōtarō Hashiguchi
Color design: Aiko Matsuyama
Director of photography: Hideki Imaizumi
Editing: Gō Sadamatsu
Sound director: Takatoshi Hamano
Sound effects: Yasumasa Koyama
Yen Press is releasing the series in English and it describes the story:

In a time when the Shadow World has taken over and most of humanity is wiped out, a party of six heroes strives and fails to save the world… But magician Desir Herman is given a second chance when he opens his eyes and finds that he's gone back thirteen years in the past! It's now up to him to gather his party once more and stop the greatest catastrophe in human history!
The first season of the anime debuted in October 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired in English-speaking, Latin America, and European countries, along with an English dub .

title: Kakao Games Announces The World of Dokkaebi MMORPG Based on Web Novel With October Launch
content:
Kakao Games announced on August 6 that it will launch Supercat's The World of Dokkaebi , a new MMORPG based on the web novel Chronicles of the Demon-Slaying Cultivator , in October.

The World of Dokkaebi combines 2D pixel-art characters with 3D environments and draws on Korean folklore and Eastern fantasy. The game is set approximately 300 years before the events of the original web novel and expands its world with new stories and characters.

The game will feature a class-free combat system that allows players to customize their abilities through skill combinations, along with guild-based cooperative content. It will be available on PC and mobile with cross-platform support.

Kakao Games also announced that actor Ji-hoon Park, who played the main character in the webtoon-based live-action series The Legend of Kitchen Soldier , has been selected as the game's official advertising model. Pre-registration began in August, with an online showcase planned for September ahead of the game's October launch in Korea.

A global launch of the game has not yet been announced.

The web novel Chronicles of the Demon-Slaying Cultivator and its webtoon adaptation both do not currently have English releases.

title: 'Ore to Yuu-nii!' Reveals Additional Staff, Teaser Promo for Winter 2027
content:
Production company DMM pictures opened an official website for a televsion anime adaptation of Miyuki Nakayama 's Shota Oni boys love manga revealed additional staff and a teaser promotional video on Friday. The anime series will premiere in January 2027.

Staff Chief Animation Director, Character Design: Yuumi Kuroiwa ( Hypnosis Mic: Division Rap Battle - Rhyme Anima + ) Art Director: Hirofune Hane ( Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 4th Season: 2-nensei-hen 1 Gakki ) Color Design: Saki Tada ( Tougen Anki ) Director of Photography: Sena Nakagawa ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun 2 ) Music: Yukari Hashimoto ( Komi-san wa, Comyushou desu. ), Ruka Kawada ( Class de 2-banme ni Kawaii Onnanoko to Tomodachi ni Natta ) Sound Director: Takeshi Takadera ( [Oshi no Ko] ) Studio: Studio Hibari

Noriko Hashimoto ( Heroine Tarumono! Kiraware Heroine to Naisho no Oshigoto ) is directing the anime, with Yuniko Ayana ( Otome Kaijuu Caraméliser ) handling the series composition.

Nakayama ( Blend S ) originally began the manga on their X (formerly Twitter) and Pixiv accounts in August 2020. Square Enix began serializing the title under its Gangan BLiss label on the Comic CMOA website in September 2021. Square Enix published the seventh volume on March 21. The manga is also available on Renta!, eBookJapan, BookLive, and Manga UP!

title: Seiji Kishi Directs Maiden Blood Original TV Anime at Polygon Pictures
content:
Pony Canyon revealed on Friday that director Seiji Kishi will direct a new original television anime series titled Maiden Blood that will debut in 2027. Pony Canyon said it will announce international release details at a later date.

The dark fantasy action anime will star Iori Saeki as Eva and Yukari Anzai as Epica.

Pony Canyon describes the series:

Armageddon—the final war between good and evil, fought at the end of the world. Its destined outcome was overturned. “I don't want to die.” That desperate wish, that hopeless human ego, gave power to the Evil God. Eight billion human beings were offered as sacrifices, and only a handful were allowed to survive, doomed to be toyed with and tormented as playthings of the Evil God. Since the dawn of the universe, the Frashokereti—the Renewal of the World—has been repeated countless times. But here, for the first time, it has failed. The sun will rise no more. In a world where the very laws of nature have gone mad, there is only one thing of value: human blood. Blood is currency. Blood is fuel. Blood is—a weapon. After countless sacrifices, the mages devised a single ritual: a forbidden art that transforms a girl's blood into a blade capable of destroying demons. Turn blood into a weapon. Turn life into a weapon. Turn humanity itself into the final weapon against the demons. The chosen… the survivors… the strongest, cursed blood warriors. Blood warriors. The younger sister, Epica, is the strongest blood warrior, her soul stolen away. The elder sister, Eva, has been unable to walk since birth. And yet, in this entire world, only one thing can awaken Epica's sleeping power: Eva's blood. Eva and Epica. Sisters bound by fate in the darkness of the end of the world. To the demons who have defiled this world—with that blood… f×cking kill them all!

Kishi ( Persona 4 , Danganronpa , Assassination Classroom , Angel Beats! ), scriptwriter Makoto Uezu ( Scum's Wish , Kengan Ashura , KONOSUBA , Yuki Yuna Is a Hero ), and Pony Canyon are credited with the original work. Keiji is directing the anime at Polygon Pictures , and Uezu is overseeing the series scripts. LAM ( Witch and Hound , takt op. Destiny , Technoroid Overmind ) is the original character designer. Composers include: Keiichi Okabe ( Yuki Yuna Is a Hero , NieR:Automata Ver 1.1a ), Kuniyuki Takahashi ( Tune In to the Midnight Heart , Death March to The Parallel World Rhapsody ), and Taichi Jōraku ( insert song for The Dark History of the Reincarnated Villainess OAV ).

Other staff members include Satoki Iida as sound director. Pony Canyon is producing the music, and MONACA is credited with music production cooperation.
author: ANN

title: Tanuki to Kitsune TV Anime Reveals Visual, October 4 Debut
content:
Frontier Works announced on Friday that the television anime based on Atamoto 's Tanuki to Kitsune (Raccoon Dog and Fox) manga will debut on October 4. The anime will air within the "Animori" program that airs on TV Tokyo and its affiliates on Sundays at 7:00 a.m. Frontier Works also revealed a key visual and the show's main staff.

Tommy Hino ( Kumarba (TV 3) , Crane Game Girls ) is directing the anime at Akatsuki Media Studio , and Rika Kihara ( Sylvanian Families Freya no Piece of Secret ) is writing the scripts.

The anime celebrates the franchise's 10th anniversary.

The manga's story centers on the daily lives of a raccoon dog who is not quite with it and a mischievous fox who likes to tease the raccoon dog. The two are close friends who live together on a mountain. Their other friends include a wolf, a bear, a rabbit, and birds.

Atamoto began serializing the manga on X (formerly Twitter ), and Frontier Works releases the manga in print. The series has already inspired a wide variety of merchandise, as well as stamps on the LINE messaging and social media app.

The franchise contains manga's 10 volumes and three picture book volumes. The second volume of a new manga series titled Tanuki to Kitsune Yurutto will ship on October 15. The overall book franchise has 1.35 million copies in circulation.

A previous series of web anime shorts debuted in February 2018.

title: Original TV Anime 'Maiden Blood' Announced for 2027
content:
Production company Pony Canyon opened an official website for the Maiden Blood original television anime on Friday, revealing the main cast, staff, a teaser visual (pictured), and teaser promotional video. The anime series will premiere in 2027.

Voice actresses Iori Saeki ( Nekopara ) and Yukari Anzai ( Watashi ga Koibito ni Nareru Wake Nai jan, Muri Muri! (※Muri ja Nakatta!?) ) are starring as Eva and Epica, respectively.

Staff Director: Seiji Kishi ( Angel Beats! Series Composition: Makoto Uezu ( Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo! ) Original Character Design: LAM ( Takt Op. Destiny ) Sound Director: Satoki Iida ( Charlotte ) Music: Keiichi Okabe ( Summertime Render ), Kuniyuki Takahashi ( Mayonaka Heart Tune ), Taichi Jouraku ( Yuusha Party ni Kawaii Ko ga Ita node, Kokuhaku shitemita. ) Music Production: Pony Canyon Music Production Cooperation: MONACA ( Bakemonogatari music) Studio: Polygon Pictures

The project began in 2020 during the pandemic, when series compositor Makoto Uezu pitched a proposal to producers for a dark, hardcore action anime entirely free of broadcasting restrictions. Inspired by the brutal aesthetic of Western RPG, the story's intense content prompted director Seiji Kishi to disclose that multiple early episode drafts were initially deemed unsuitable for television broadcast. The production committee remains in ongoing negotiations with broadcasting networks to ensure the uncompromising dark fantasy narrative can be televised as originally intended.

Synopsis Armageddon has overturned the world's destiny, where an Evil God has risen after gaining power from the ego of humans who feared death. As a result, eight billion people were sacrificed, leaving only a handful of survivors to exist merely as playthings for the god in a world shrouded in eternal darkness. In this twisted world where logic is gone, human blood has become everything—from currency and fuel to a forbidden weapon forged by sorcerers to eradicate demons.

Eva and Epica are a pair of sisters bound by a tragic fate in the midst of this apocalypse. The younger sister, Eva, is the ultimate blood-battle human who has lost her soul, while the older sister, Epica, was born unable to walk. However, only Epica's blood can awaken Eva's power to fight against the demons that have defiled the world.

title: Magical Girl Raising Project restart Anime Debuts on October 5
content:
Hiroyuki Hashimoto returns from the first Magical Girl Raising Project anime as the director. Takao Yoshioka is returning to write the script. Masako Itou ( Magical Girl Raising Project SD character designer) is designing the characters for the new anime based on original designs by Maruino . Satoki Iida is returning as sound director. Synergy SP is the new animation studio, replacing Lerche that animated the previous Magical Girl Raising Project anime. Minori Chihara performs the anime's opening theme song "No tears here." Daisy×Daisy performs the ending theme song "ReMind."

The first 12-episode Magical Girl Raising Project anime premiered in Japan on the AT-X channel in October 2016, and Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired.

Endō's Mahō Shōjo Ikusei Keikaku light novel series is set in a world where a social game called The Magical Girl Raising Project allows one in tens of thousands of people to be a "magical girl" — possessing extraordinary physical capabilities and looks, as well as special magical powers that set them apart from the rest of the human race. But one day, in a district containing 16 magical girls, the administration announces that it must halve the number of magical girls to solve the problem of magical energy. At first, the 16 magical girls race to collect more "magical candy" than their competitors, but the rules quickly become twisted, and it quickly becomes a murderous battle for survival among them.
